clue.text: These officers end by leaving James Brydon out

indicators.note: leaving tells us the letters of end by are taken away from the name before it is rearranged
out signals the remaining letters are put out of order, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Some army officers wind up excluding a man called James Brydon from their circle.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: JAMES BRYDON holds the letters of END BY plus the answer, so strike those five and rearrange the rest. The names in this puzzle belong to crossword setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Majors are commissioned army officers ranking above captain, so a plural noun fits 'These officers'.

clue.text: Low gear involved finding place to leave a boat

explanation.definitionFit: A moorage is a place where a boat can be moored, or the fee for mooring there.

clue.text: Biblical character involved with downs for John Dawson

explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: JOHN DAWSON holds the letters of DOWNS plus the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonah is the Old Testament prophet swallowed by a great fish.

clue.text: Removes all traces of sport contest around square

S is short for square, as in street names

explanation.definitionFit: To rub out is to erase completely, removing every trace of something.

clue.text: Stallholder's cart causing pub brawl?

explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a small handcart of the kind costermongers and market stallholders sell from.

clue.text: Princess has limits to awful temper

indicators.note: limits to means the outermost letters of the next word

clue.text: Part with toy, perhaps one to follow?

explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look up to and copy, someone to follow.

clue.text: Straw breaking camel's back, doubly profligate

the back of camel, taken doubly, means its last two letters

explanation.surface: The proverbial last straw, which broke the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a spendthrift who squanders money, so a profligate as a noun.

clue.text: Simple language from bird heard on the Big Breakfast?

a full English is the big British cooked breakfast of bacon, eggs and sausages

explanation.definitionFit: Pidgin English is a simplified contact language mixing English with local tongues, used for basic trade talk.

clue.text: See 23

clue.text: Instruction to reader remains in Asian language

clue.text: Lawn cut by waters in Lake District village

cut means the word for lawn loses its final letter, like a trimmed edge

a mere is a lake or pond, a body of water

has ignored says the letters of Maria are left out of the name's pool

clue.text: Ill-fated ship in French tributary of the Rhone

the Durance is a river in Provence flowing into the Rhone

clue.text: Consecrates Keynes having abandoned Ashley Knowles at sea

clue.text: Broken the ulna? Hospital by end of the day in a bad condition

clue.text: Money paid out to former US vice-president, we're told

clue.text: Rumour that Sarah Hayes has lost out

out signals the remaining letters are put out of order

clue.text: Educate artists and porpoises as a group!

the collective noun for porpoises, dolphins and fish

clue.text: Areas which take their toll
